authorities.title_or_locator: Code on Unit Trusts and Mutual Funds, section 6.8; supplied excerpts require applicable version and scope.
Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular, where applicable.
26EC22, complete paragraphs 10–13 incorporated by footnote 5, with associated footnotes including footnote 2.
Parts A and B of the Appendix to the circular containing intermediary paragraphs 17–18, if that intermediary scope applies.

claims.action: Retain ultimate responsibility for management and operational soundness of the adopted tokenisation arrangement
claims.statement: Product Providers should remain ultimately responsible for management and operational soundness of the adopted tokenisation arrangement, regardless of outsourcing.
uncertainty: The excerpt does not prescribe a complete test for fulfillment or specify the allocation of particular decision-making powers.

claims.action: Retain ultimate responsibility for ownership record keeping
claims.statement: Product Providers should remain ultimately responsible for ownership record keeping, regardless of outsourcing.

claims.action: Preserve full responsibility despite outsourcing
conditions: An outsourcing arrangement exists, including one envisaged under section 6.8.
claims.statement: Outsourcing, including arrangements envisaged under section 6.8, does not remove the Product Provider's full responsibility.
uncertainty: Retention of responsibility does not itself establish exclusive performance or exclusive operational authority.

claims.action: Identify public-offering context
claims.statement: Footnote 1 grounds retained responsibility in these products being offered to the public in Hong Kong and the importance of proper records reflecting investors' ownership.
uncertainty: The excerpt does not establish the complete instrument's applicability to other products.

claims.action: Refer to applicable tokenisation factors
conditions: The Part A factors are applicable.
claims.statement: When formulating the tokenisation arrangement, Product Providers are directed to Part A of the Appendix to the Tokenised Securities Circular for applicable factors of consideration.
uncertainty: The factors themselves are not supplied.

claims.action: Ensure proper ownership records are maintained
claims.statement: Product Providers should ensure maintenance of proper records of token holders' ownership interests in the product.
uncertainty: Footnote 2 is absent; the complete standard for proper records is not supplied.

claims.action: Ensure operational compatibility
claims.statement: Product Providers should ensure that the tokenisation arrangement is operationally compatible with the service providers involved.
uncertainty: Footnote 2 may qualify this requirement but is not supplied.

claims.action: Confirm the specified matters
claims.statement: On the ordinary grammatical reading of paragraph 14, Product Providers should confirm management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity without waiting for an SFC request.
uncertainty: Footnote 5 identifies the SFC as recipient of confirmation and demonstration. Whether 'to the SFC's satisfaction' also qualifies confirmation, rather than demonstration alone, remains an attachment question.

claims.action: Demonstrate the specified matters to the SFC's satisfaction
claims.statement: Upon the SFC's request, Product Providers should demonstrate to its satisfaction management and operational soundness of the arrangement, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity.
uncertainty: No response deadline or detailed satisfaction standard is supplied.

claims.action: Confirm and demonstrate minimum compliance
conditions: Read with paragraph 14's request trigger for demonstration.
claims.statement: Footnote 5 specifies that confirmation and demonstration to the SFC should cover, at a minimum, compliance with paragraphs 10–13.
uncertainty: The full incorporated requirements are unavailable; this minimum is not an exhaustive satisfaction standard.

claims.action: Confirm and demonstrate absence of smart-contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with high confidence
conditions: Read with paragraph 14's request trigger for demonstration.
claims.statement: Footnote 5 includes, at a minimum, confirmation and demonstration that smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws, with a high level of confidence.
uncertainty: The text supplies no numerical confidence threshold or testing method. The confidence phrase most directly qualifies the smart-contract proposition, but a broader attachment to the coordinated minimum showing is possible.

claims.action: Identify competing trigger readings
claims.statement: Reading the paragraph and footnote together supports unconditional confirmation and request-triggered demonstration, with footnote 5 specifying their minimum content. Read independently, footnote 5's unqualified pairing of confirmation and demonstration could support an ongoing demonstration requirement; that reading must be reconciled with paragraph 14's express trigger.
temporal: SFC request is expressly attached to demonstration in paragraph 14.
uncertainty: The supplied excerpts do not conclusively resolve the apparent tension; treating the request as a condition of confirmation as well is less supported by paragraph 14's syntax.

claims.action: Identify consequences of no SFC request
conditions: No relevant SFC request has been made.
Paragraph 14 and footnote 5 are read together as specifying a request-triggered demonstration.
claims.statement: Absent a relevant request, the express triggers for paragraph 14 demonstration, paragraph 15 third-party audit or verification, and paragraph 16 legal opinion have not occurred. This does not remove confirmation or underlying responsibilities, or establish compliance or SFC satisfaction.
temporal: While no relevant request has been made.
uncertainty: The rival independent reading of footnote 5 remains unresolved; no general exemption from assurance requirements elsewhere follows.

claims.action: Obtain third-party audit or verification
claims.statement: Under paragraph 15, Product Providers should obtain third-party audit or verification on management and operational soundness, ownership record keeping and smart-contract integrity upon SFC request.
uncertainty: The provision does not say that every paragraph 14 demonstration must use a third-party audit or verification.

claims.action: Obtain a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application
claims.statement: Under paragraph 16, Product Providers should obtain a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application upon SFC request.
uncertainty: The opinion's required subject matter and satisfaction criteria are not specified; it is not stated to substitute for paragraph 15 assurance.

claims.action: Maintain a register of holders
claims.actor: The scheme or, for a unit trust, the trustee or person appointed by the trustee
claims.statement: Section 6.8 requires the scheme or, for a unit trust, the trustee or its appointed person to maintain a register of holders.
uncertainty: This allocation of record-maintenance performance does not displace the Product Provider's responsibility under footnote 1.

claims.action: Advise the Commission of register locations
claims.actor: Responsible actor under section 6.8; the notification sentence does not expressly name one
claims.statement: The Commission must be advised on request of the addresses where the register is kept.
uncertainty: The passive wording leaves the notifying actor implicit.

claims.action: Exercise reasonable care, skill and diligence in selecting, appointing and monitoring a valuation third party
conditions: A third party is engaged in valuation of a scheme.
claims.statement: Section 6.11C requires reasonable care, skill and diligence in selection, appointment and ongoing monitoring to ensure the valuation third party has appropriate knowledge, experience and resources commensurate with each scheme's valuation policies and procedures.
temporal: At selection and appointment and during ongoing monitoring.
uncertainty: This express valuation standard is not expressly incorporated as the standard for paragraph 10 tokenisation responsibility.

claims.action: Supervise and review third-party valuation activities
conditions: A third party is engaged in valuation of a scheme.
claims.statement: The management company should subject the third party's valuation activities to ongoing supervision and periodic review.
uncertainty: This is a scoped supervisory-conduct rule, not a supplied general safe harbour for tokenisation responsibility.

claims.action: Retain responsibility for overall tokenisation operation
claims.actor: Intermediaries issuing or substantially involved in issuing Tokenised Securities
conditions: They intend to deal in or advise on those Tokenised Securities.
claims.statement: Intermediary paragraph 13 states that qualifying issuers or substantially involved intermediaries remain responsible for overall operation of the tokenisation arrangement notwithstanding outsourcing.
uncertainty: Whether a particular Product Provider also falls within this intermediary scope requires facts. This paragraph 13 is not established to be the paragraph 13 incorporated by footnote 5.

claims.action: Conduct due diligence on issuers, tokenisation service providers, features and risks
conditions: They deal in, advise on, or manage portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities.
claims.statement: Paragraph 17 reminds qualifying intermediaries to conduct due diligence on issuers and tokenisation vendors or service providers, and on features and risks arising from the arrangement.
uncertainty: The supplied reminder does not expressly use must or should; its precise underlying modality and application to a Product Provider require the applicable instrument and facts.

claims.action: Understand and be satisfied with ownership and technology risk controls
conditions: They deal in, advise on, or manage portfolios investing in Tokenised Securities.
claims.statement: Qualifying intermediaries should understand and be satisfied with issuer and service-provider controls managing ownership and technology risks before engaging in related activities.
uncertainty: This actor-specific conduct requirement does not establish fulfillment of the Product Provider's distinct responsibility.

claims.action: Consult non-exhaustive factors
claims.statement: The intermediary provisions direct readers to Parts A and B of the circular's Appendix for a non-exhaustive list of factors for consideration.
uncertainty: The Appendix is absent; its factors cannot be treated as an exhaustive compliance test.

uncertainties: No actual outsourcing contracts, allocations of authority, oversight records, operational evidence, ownership records, smart-contract assessments, confirmation communications or SFC requests are supplied. No finding of fulfillment or breach can therefore be made.

A defensible assessment must distinguish retained accountability and supporting authority arrangements, supervisory conduct in practice, and operational and ownership-record outcomes. Evidence of one category alone does not establish the other categories. The excerpts do not specify which powers must be retained or a complete sufficiency test.

Paragraph 10 supports both an emphasis on non-transferable accountability and a broader reading requiring substantive discharge of responsibility for soundness and records. It does not resolve whether particular failures establish noncompliance irrespective of care, or whether an applicable conduct standard governs fulfillment. Neither a strict outcome guarantee nor a reasonable-care safe harbour is established.

Section 6.11C expressly supplies a care and supervision standard for outsourced valuation. Its standard cannot automatically be transferred to tokenisation; any application or analogy requires justification.

Paragraph 14 most naturally conditions demonstration alone on request. Footnote 5's unqualified wording creates a rival reading concerning demonstration, while also clarifying the recipient and minimum content. The scope of SFC satisfaction over confirmation and the scope of the high-confidence qualifier remain interpretive questions.

No SFC request does not establish approval, satisfaction, absence of vulnerabilities or compliance. It leaves underlying responsibility and the ordinary reading of the confirmation requirement intact.

The full applicable 26EC22 instrument, paragraphs 10–13, footnote 2 and incorporated Appendix factors are unavailable. The packet does not establish instrument versions, complete definitions or applicability to a particular entity or product.

Paragraphs 15 and 16 specify different request-triggered deliverables: technical or operational third-party assurance and a satisfactory legal opinion supporting the application. Neither is stated to substitute for the other or automatically discharge paragraph 14.

The supplied intermediary paragraph 13 belongs to a separately described intermediary context; matching paragraph numbers do not establish that it satisfies footnote 5's incorporation of paragraphs 10–13.

units.rationale: Core retained-responsibility provision; separates operational responsibility from ownership record keeping.
Footnote preserves responsibility despite outsourcing, supplies public-offering context and incorporates applicable Appendix factors.
Adds substantive record-maintenance and compatibility outcomes; missing footnote 2 is a qualification gap.
Separates confirmation from request-triggered demonstration and identifies objects and satisfaction standard.
Footnote supplies minimum content, recipient and confidence language while creating a trigger-attachment question.
Separate request-triggered legal opinion supporting the application.
Identifies the section 6.8 register-maintenance actor; duplicated in the next fuller excerpt.
Adds request-triggered location notification to the register-maintenance rule.
Express conduct standard for outsourced valuation provides a relevant comparison, but no supplied incorporation makes it the paragraph 10 tokenisation standard.
Potentially overlapping intermediary responsibility; applicability requires role and activity facts and is not inferred from paragraph numbering.
Potentially applicable intermediary conduct, prior-activity timing and non-exhaustive incorporated factors; kept distinct from Product Provider fulfillment.
